topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: It provides introductory framing and historical context for the lecture on the complement system.

topics.label: Fundamentals of the complement system and C3 activation
topics.groupedBecause: They establish the foundational principles, naming conventions, and central molecular activation mechanism of the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: They detail the recognition and activation mechanisms of the alternative, lectin, and classical pathways that drive complement deposition on target surfaces.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: They explain the downstream effector functions through which activated complement eradicates pathogens and promotes the immune response.

topics.label: Host cell regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: It examines the regulatory mechanisms and proteins that protect host cells from accidental complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It describes how specific genetic or acquired defects at different stages of the complement cascade lead to distinct disease phenotypes.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement and applications of protein A
topics.groupedBecause: It explores how pathogens circumvent complement-mediated killing and how these bacterial evasion mechanisms are utilized in research and therapy.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: It closes the lecture on complement and provides a brief forward reference to the next session.
